newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Perez Companc hopes for more in Venezuela oil sale.
newsitem.headline: Perez Companc hopes for more in Venezuela oil sale.

text.p: Argentina's Perez Companc, which offered Tuesday the highest bid yet in Venezuela's third oil auction round, will continue to bid in future sales for what it sees as excellent local opportunities.
"If you look at the geological risk (here), it is the best in the continent ... you can make some money," company vice president Walter Schmale told Reuters.
"We want to win all that we can, but we're competing with some very big companies," he added.

Perez Companc, which has a ninety percent share in a consortium with William Companies Inc, bid $153 million Tuesday morning for the 20 year contract to operate the La Concepcion field on Lake Maracaibo.
The bid was $26 million more than the next highest offer.
"We paid that much because that's what we think the field is worth," the company's Venezuelan president Horacio Begaries said.
On Monday, Perez Companc in association with Corporacion Corepli de Venezuela, also bid $41 million for the Acema field -- edging ahead of the nearest offer by a mere $22.
"We're going to keep on participating (in the auctions)," Schmale said.
The company already has operations at the San Carlos and Oritupano-Leona fields.
Williams Companies Inc meanwhile has a gas management contract at the Furrial field in eastern Venezuela.
